decision: Is there enough pipeline to hit the target, and should we build pipeline, advance deals or improve conversion?
limitations: The forecast is only as good as the stage probabilities. Optimistic ones give a wish, not a forecast; take them from real conversion history and mark them as assumed if not.
A deal whose stage name doesn't exactly match the probability map (case matters) counts at 0% with only a warning, which lowers the forecast and raises the early-stage share.
Required coverage is 1 divided by your win rate, and commit is deals at 75% or more. A wrong win rate moves the coverage verdict and the new-pipeline figure together.
It has no close dates, so it treats every open deal as closable this period. Best case and coverage overstate what can land if deals are slipping.
review: The sales lead checks each deal's stage, the stage probabilities against historical conversion, and the win rate before the forecast goes to the board. Report commit and best case separately.
